title.zh: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 39: Gan Wenkun, Fan Chengmo, Ma Xiongzhen, Fu Honglie
title.raw: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈

sentences.zh: 列傳三十九

translations.literal: Biographies 39
translations.idiomatic: Biography 39

sentences.zh: =甘文焜=甘文焜，字炳如，漢軍正藍旗人，其先自豐城徙瀋陽。

translations.literal: Gan Wenkun. Gan Wenkun, whose style name was Bingru, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner; his forebears had moved from Fengcheng to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenkun, styled Bingru, belonged to the Han division of the Plain Blue Banner; his family had moved from Fengcheng to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 父應魁，從入關，官至石匣副將。

translations.literal: His father Yingkui followed [the Qing] in entering the Pass and reached the post of deputy commander at Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingkui entered China with the Qing forces and eventually became deputy commander at Shixia.

sentences.zh: 文焜善騎射，喜讀書，尤慕古忠孝事。

translations.literal: Wenkun was skilled at mounted archery, delighted in reading, and especially admired ancient tales of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun excelled at horsemanship and archery, loved books, and was especially drawn to stories of ancient loyalty and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 以官學生授兵部筆帖式，累遷禮部啟心郎，屢奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: As a government student he was appointed a clerical secretary in the Board of War, was promoted in succession to Qixin Lang in the Board of Rites, and on repeated missions won praise as meeting the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Through the government student program he became a clerk in the Ministry of War, rose to Qixin Lang in the Ministry of Rites, and on diplomatic missions repeatedly pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授大理寺少卿，遷順天府府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and was transferred to be Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he became vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 崇文門榷稅不平，疏劾之。

translations.literal: The transit duties at Chongwen Gate were levied unfairly, and he memorialized impeaching [the officials responsible].
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against the unfair transit tax collection at Chongwen Gate.

sentences.zh: 廷議令兼攝，文焜曰：「言之而居之，是利之也。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and ordered him to take the post concurrently; Wenkun said, "To speak out and then hold the office oneself is to profit from it."
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed that he take over the tax post himself; Wenkun said, "To denounce an office and then occupy it is to turn the denunciation into profit."

sentences.zh: 」固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，授直隸巡撫，奏复巡歷舊制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Zhili and memorialized to restore the former practice of touring inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was named governor of Zhili and memorialized to restore the old custom of provincial inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 單車按部，適保定、真定所屬諸縣患水災，疏請蠲歲賦。

translations.literal: He went through his jurisdiction in a single cart; it happened that the counties under Baoding and Zhending suffered flood disasters, and he memorialized requesting remission of the annual tax.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling alone by cart on his rounds, he found floods afflicting the counties under Baoding and Zhending and memorialized for exemption of that year's land tax.

sentences.zh: 總督白秉真以賑費浩繁，請聽官民輸銀米。

translations.literal: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, because relief expenses were vast, requested permission to allow officials and commoners to contribute silver and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, citing the enormous cost of relief, asked that officials and civilians be allowed to donate silver and grain.

sentences.zh: 文焜斥廉俸以助。

translations.literal: Wenkun drew on his clean stipend salary to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun contributed from his official salary to help.

sentences.zh: 議敘，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On review of merit he was given an additional appointment as Vice Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His service was recognized with an additional post as vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷雲貴總督，駐貴陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be Governor-General of Yunnan-Guizhou and was stationed at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, with his seat at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂鎮雲南，欲藉邊釁固兵權，詭報土番康東入寇，紿文焜移師，又陰嗾凱里諸苗乘其後。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui held Yunnan and wished to use border incidents to consolidate military power; he falsely reported that the aboriginal tribe Kangdong had invaded, tricked Wenkun into moving troops, and secretly incited the Miao of Kaili to strike from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui then controlled Yunnan and sought pretexts on the frontier to keep his armies; he fabricated an invasion by the Kangdong tribes, lured Wenkun to move his forces, and secretly stirred the Kaili Miao to attack from the rear.

sentences.zh: 文焜策康東無能為，凱里近肘腋，不制將滋蔓，先督兵搗其巢，斬苗酋阿戎。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged that Kangdong could do nothing, but that Kaili was close at the armpit and if not checked would spread; he first led troops to storm their nest and beheaded the Miao chief Arong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun concluded that Kangdong posed no real threat but that Kaili lay too close to ignore; if left alone the trouble would spread, so he led troops first to destroy their stronghold and killed the Miao leader Arong.

sentences.zh: 既平，約雲南會剿康東。

translations.literal: Once pacified, he arranged with Yunnan for a joint campaign against Kangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After that victory he arranged a joint campaign with Yunnan against Kangdong.

sentences.zh: 三桂慮詐洩，謂康東已遠遁，繇是益憚之。

translations.literal: Sangui feared his deception would leak out, claimed Kangdong had fled far away, and from this feared Wenkun all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui, afraid his deception would be exposed, claimed Kangdong had already fled, and from then on feared Wenkun even more.

sentences.zh: 文焜巡歷雲、貴各府州皆遍。

translations.literal: Wenkun toured every prefecture and department of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun made inspection tours through every prefecture and sub-prefecture in Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，遭母憂，上命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he suffered mourning for his mother; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 文焜又遣兵擊殺臻剖苗酋阿福。

translations.literal: Wenkun again sent troops to attack and kill Ah Fu, the Miao chief of Zhenpo.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun also sent troops who killed Ah Fu, chief of the Zhenpo Miao.

sentences.zh: 疏乞歸葬，許給假治喪。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to return to bury [his mother]; leave to conduct funeral rites was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to return home for the burial and was granted leave to perform the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 三桂請以雲南巡撫兼督篆，令督標兵悉詣雲南受節度，而以利啗之，冀為己用。

translations.literal: Sangui requested that he concurrently hold the seal as Yunnan Governor, ordered all the troops of the governor-general's banner to go to Yunnan to receive command, and tried to entice him with profit, hoping to use him for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui asked that Wenkun also serve as Yunnan governor, ordered the governor-general's banner troops to Yunnan to serve under his command, and tried to win him with favors, hoping to make him his own man.

sentences.zh: 十二年，文焜還本官，適撤籓議起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wenkun returned to his original office; just then the plan to abolish princely domains arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wenkun resumed his former post just as the court began debating the abolition of the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，殺巡撫硃國治，遣其黨偪貴陽。

translations.literal: Sangui rebelled, killed Governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his agents to press on Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui revolted, murdered Governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his forces against Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 文焜聞變，使族弟文炯齎奏入告，牒貴州提督李本深率兵扼盤江。

translations.literal: Hearing of the uprising, Wenkun had his cousin Wenjiong carry a memorial to the capital to report, and sent a dispatch to Guizhou Military Commander Li Benshen to lead troops to hold Pan River.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the revolt, Wenkun sent his cousin Wenjiong to the capital with a memorial and ordered Guizhou commander Li Benshen to hold the Pan River line.

sentences.zh: 本深已懷貳，先以書覘文焜意。

translations.literal: Benshen already harbored disloyal intentions and first sent a letter to probe Wenkun's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Li Benshen was already disloyal and first sent a letter to sound Wenkun out.

sentences.zh: 文焜手書報之，期效張巡、南霽雲誓死守，而本深不之顧。

translations.literal: Wenkun wrote back by hand, expecting to imitate Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun in vowing to defend to the death, but Benshen paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun wrote back pledging to die like Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun, but Benshen ignored him.

sentences.zh: 本標兵已受三桂餌，紛潰弗聽調。

translations.literal: Benshen's banner troops had already accepted Sangui's bribes and scattered in defeat, refusing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Benshen's troops had taken Wu's bribes and broke ranks, refusing all orders.

sentences.zh: 文焜度貴陽不可守，令妾盛率婦女七人自經死，獨攜第四子國城赴鎮遠，思召湖北兵扼險隘，使賊不北出。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged Guiyang could not be held, ordered his concubine Sheng to lead seven women to hang themselves, and alone took his fourth son Guocheng to Zhenyuan, thinking to summon Hubei troops to hold the passes and prevent the rebels from moving north.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Guiyang indefensible, he had his concubine Sheng and seven other women hang themselves, then went alone with his fourth son Guocheng toward Zhenyuan, hoping to bring Hubei troops to block the passes and keep the rebels from marching north.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申朔，癸卯至鎮遠，守將江義已受偽命，拒弗納。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, bingchen day of the new moon, on guimao he reached Zhenyuan; the defending commander Jiang Yi had already accepted a rebel commission and refused to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Zhenyuan on guimao, the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month; the garrison commander Jiang Yi had already accepted a rebel commission and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 文焜渡河至吉祥寺，義遣兵圍之。

translations.literal: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple; Yi sent troops to surround him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple, and Jiang Yi sent troops to surround him.

sentences.zh: 文焜望闕再拜，拔佩刀將自殺，國城大呼請先死，奪其刀以刎而還之，屍乃踣，血濺文焜衣。

translations.literal: Wenkun bowed toward the palace twice, drew his sword to kill himself; Guocheng shouted asking to die first, seized the blade and cut his own throat then returned it, the body fell, blood splashing Wenkun's clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun bowed toward the capital, drew his sword to kill himself; Guocheng cried that he should die first, seized the blade, cut his own throat, and fell—his blood splashing his father's robe.

sentences.zh: 文焜曰：「是兒勇過我！

translations.literal: Wenkun said, "This boy is braver than I!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun said, "The boy was braver than I!"

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺，年四十有二。

translations.literal: Then he killed himself; he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed himself. He was forty-two.

sentences.zh: 從者筆帖式和善雅圖殉。

translations.literal: His attendant clerk Heshanyatu died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His clerk Heshanyatu died with him.

sentences.zh: 亂平，貴州巡撫楊雍建以文焜治績及死事狀上聞，予優恤。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, Guizhou Governor Yang Yongjian reported Wenkun's administration and death to the throne; favorable condolence was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, Guizhou governor Yang Yongjian reported Wenkun's record and martyrdom; the court granted exceptional posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 遣其長子宣化同知國均迎喪還京師，使內大臣佟國維迎奠盧溝橋，贈兵部尚書，諡忠果。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guojun, Tongzhi of Xuanhua, was sent to bring the coffin back to the capital; Inner Minister Tong Guowei was sent to receive and offer libation at Lugou Bridge; he was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous title Zhongguo (Loyal and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guojun, sub-prefect of Xuanhua, was sent to bring the body home; Inner Minister Tong Guowei received the coffin at Lugou Bridge; Wenkun was posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous name Zhongguo (Loyal Resolute).

sentences.zh: 建祠貴陽，上賜「勁節」二字顏其額。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Guiyang; the emperor bestowed the two characters "Steadfast Integrity" to inscribe its tablet.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was erected in Guiyang, and the emperor inscribed its gate with the words "Steadfast Integrity."

sentences.zh: 子七，國璧尤知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Guobi was especially well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Guobi was especially renowned.

sentences.zh: 國璧，字東屏，以任子授陝州知州，改蘇州同知，擢山西平陽、浙江寧波知府，名循吏。

translations.literal: Guobi, style Dongping, through hereditary appointment received Zhizhou of Shanzhou, was changed to Tongzhi of Suzhou, was promoted to Prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang—renowned as an exemplary official.
translations.idiomatic: Guobi, styled Dongping, entered office by hereditary privilege as prefect of Shanzhou, later served as Suzhou sub-prefect, then became prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang, winning renown as a model local administrator.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，幸杭州，御書硃子詩及「永貞」額以賜。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor on his southern tour visited Hangzhou and bestowed an imperial poem in vermilion ink and a plaque reading "Ever Faithful."
translations.idiomatic: On his southern tour the Kangxi Emperor visited Hangzhou and presented him with an imperial poem in the emperor's own vermilion hand and a plaque reading "Ever Faithful."

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「汝父盡節，朕未嘗忘，此為汝母書也。

translations.literal: He instructed: "Your father died for integrity; I have not forgotten—this is written for your mother."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your father died loyal; I have never forgotten. This inscription is for your mother."

sentences.zh: 」累遷雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，起為正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was recalled as Commander-in-Chief of the Han Army of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was recalled as commander of the Han division of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，授綏遠城右翼副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed Right Deputy Commander at Suiyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year three he became deputy commander of the right wing at Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 复罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed again.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: =范承謨=范承謨，字覲公，漢軍鑲黃旗人，文程次子。

translations.literal: Fan Chengmo. Fan Chengmo, whose style name was Jingong, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, the second son of Fan Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengmo, styled Jingong, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and the second son of Fan Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，選庶吉士，授弘文院編修。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed Compiler in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi year nine, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and became a compiler in the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to become a secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed Governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year seven he became governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時去開國未久，民流亡未復業，浙東寧波、金華等六府荒田尤多。

translations.literal: At the time it was not long since the founding of the dynasty; the people were displaced and had not returned to cultivation; in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures Ningbo, Jinhua, and others had especially much wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was still young; refugees had not yet returned to their farms, and in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures including Ningbo and Jinhua held vast tracts of abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 總督趙廷臣請除賦額，上命承謨履勘。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen requested reduction of the tax quota; the emperor ordered Chengmo to conduct an on-site survey.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen asked to reduce tax quotas; the throne ordered Chengmo to inspect the land in person.

sentences.zh: 承謨遍歷諸府，請免荒田及水沖田地賦凡三十一萬五千五百馀畝。

translations.literal: Chengmo toured all the prefectures and requested exemption of tax on wasteland and flood-washed fields totaling more than 315,500 mu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo toured every prefecture and requested tax exemptions on more than 315,500 mu of abandoned or flood-ruined fields.

sentences.zh: 杭州、嘉興、湖州、紹興四府被水，民飢，承謨出布政使庫銀八萬，糴米湖廣平糶，最貧者得附老弱例，肩鹽給朝夕，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: The four prefectures Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing suffered flood; the people were starving; Chengmo took 80,000 taels from the provincial treasurer's vault, bought grain in Huguang and sold it at fair price; the poorest were allowed under the precedent for the aged and infirm to carry salt for their daily food—very many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing; Chengmo spent eighty thousand taels from the provincial treasury to buy grain in Huguang and sell it at fair prices, and allowed the poorest families to work under the salt-carrier exemption for the aged—saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 並疏請「漕米改折，石銀一兩。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting: "Convert grain tribute to cash payment, one tael per picul."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Convert grain tribute to a cash levy of one tael per picul."

sentences.zh: 明年麥熟，補徵白糧，以三年帶徵。

translations.literal: "Next year when wheat ripens, make up collection of white rice, to be levied over three years in arrears."
translations.idiomatic: "When the wheat ripens next year, collect the white-rice quota in arrears over three years."

sentences.zh: 災重者如例蠲免」。

translations.literal: "Those with severe disaster to be exempted as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: "Where the disaster was severe, grant exemptions as usual."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: He received imperial approval to implement.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and ordered these measures carried out.

sentences.zh: 十年，以疾請解職，召還。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because of illness he requested dismissal and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to resign for illness and was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 總督劉兆麒、提督塞白理疏言浙民請留承謨一百五十馀牒，給事中姜希轍、柯聳，御史何元英等亦言：「承謨受事三載，愛民如子，不通請謁饋遺。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and Military Commander Sa Baili memorialized that the people of Zhejiang had submitted more than 150 petitions asking to retain Chengmo; Censors Jiang Xizhe and Ke Song, Investigating Censor He Yuanying, and others also said: "Chengmo has held office three years, loves the people as his children, and does not accept visits, petitions, or gifts."
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and commander Sa Baili reported that Zhejiang commoners had submitted more than 150 petitions begging Chengmo to stay; supervising secretaries Jiang Xizhe and Ke Song, censor He Yuanying, and others wrote: "In three years in office Chengmo has loved the people like his own children and refused all lobbying and gifts."

sentences.zh: 劾罷貪墨，廉治巨猾，剔除加耗、陋規、私派諸弊。

translations.literal: He impeached and dismissed the corrupt, governed with integrity against great rascals, and eliminated the abuses of surcharges, improper fees, and private levies.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached corrupt officials, punished major wrongdoers with integrity, and abolished surcharges, illicit fees, and unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: 浙民愛戴，深於飢渴。

translations.literal: The people of Zhejiang love and esteem him more deeply than hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhejiang cherish him as they would food and water in famine.

sentences.zh: 」上命承謨留任。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chengmo to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chengmo to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，承謨复疏言湖、嘉兩府白糧加耗，多寡不一，請每石加四斗五升為限；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chengmo again memorialized that the surcharges on white rice in Huzhou and Jiaxing varied in amount and requested a limit of four dou and five sheng added per picul;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chengmo memorialized again that surcharges on white-rice tribute in Huzhou and Jiaxing varied wildly and asked that they be capped at four dou five sheng per picul;

sentences.zh: 又奏蠲溫、台二衛康熙九年以前逋賦及石門、平陽未完輕齎月糧：皆下戶部議行。

translations.literal: he also memorialized to remit arrears before the ninth year of Kangxi for the two guards Wenzhou and Taizhou and unfinished light-transport monthly grain for Shimen and Pingyang—all were sent to the Board of Revenue for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to remit pre-Kangxi-9 arrears for the Wenzhou and Taizhou guards and unpaid light-transport monthly grain quotas for Shimen and Pingyang—all referred to the Ministry of Revenue for enactment.

sentences.zh: 十月，擢福建總督，疏辭未允，請入覲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to Governor-General of Fujian; his memorial declining was not accepted, and he requested an audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian; his refusal was denied, and he asked to come to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，至京師，入對。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached the capital and had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached the capital and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 承謨疾未癒，命御醫診視，賜藥餌。

translations.literal: Chengmo's illness had not yet healed; the emperor ordered imperial physicians to examine him and bestowed medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo was still ill; the emperor sent court physicians to treat him and gave him medicine.

sentences.zh: 疾稍差，趣赴官，賜冠服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: When his illness improved slightly, he was urged to take up his post; he was granted official cap and robe and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved slightly, he was urged to take up his post and was given court dress and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 福建總督初駐漳州，至是以將撤籓，命移駐福州。

translations.literal: The Fujian governor-general had initially been stationed at Zhangzhou; at this time because the feudatories were to be abolished, he was ordered to move his seat to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian governor-general had first been stationed at Zhangzhou; now, with the feudatories about to be abolished, he was ordered to move his seat to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，承謨察精忠有異志，時方議裁兵，承謨疏請緩行。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; Chengmo perceived that Jingzhong harbored disloyal intentions; at the time troops were being discussed for reduction, and Chengmo memorialized requesting delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengmo saw that Geng Jingzhong harbored treasonous designs; as the court debated troop reductions, Chengmo memorialized to slow the process.

sentences.zh: 又報巡歷邊海，欲置身外郡，便徵調防禦。

translations.literal: He also reported touring the coastal border, wishing to place himself in outer prefectures to facilitate mobilization for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported touring the coast, planning to station himself in outlying prefectures where he could more easily call up troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 事未行而精忠叛，陽言海寇至，約承謨計事。

translations.literal: Before this could be carried out Jingzhong rebelled, falsely claiming sea bandits had arrived, and invited Chengmo to consult on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could act, Geng Jingzhong rebelled, pretended that pirates had arrived, and summoned Chengmo to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉秉政附精忠，趣同行。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingzheng sided with Jingzhong and urged him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingzheng had joined the rebels and pressed Chengmo to go with him.

sentences.zh: 承謨知有變，左右請擐甲從，承謨曰：「眾寡不敵，備無益也。

translations.literal: Chengmo knew something had changed; those around him asked to don armor and follow; Chengmo said, "We are too few to match them; preparations would be useless."
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo knew treachery was afoot; his attendants urged him to arm himself, but Chengmo said, "We are outnumbered; armor would do no good."

sentences.zh: 」遂往。

translations.literal: He then went.
translations.idiomatic: He went anyway.

sentences.zh: 精忠之徒露刃相脅，承謨挺身前，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's followers bared blades to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Geng's men drew their swords to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and cursed them without stopping.

sentences.zh: 精忠拘之土室，加以桎梏，絕粒十日，不得死。

translations.literal: Jingzhong confined him in an earthen chamber, put him in stocks, and cut off food for ten days, yet he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Geng imprisoned him in a cell, put him in stocks, and starved him for ten days, yet he would not die.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣秉政說降，承謨奮足蹴之僕，叱左右掖之出，曰：「賊就僇當不遠，我先褫其魄！

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent Bingzheng to persuade him to surrender; Chengmo kicked with his foot and knocked Bingzheng down, shouted for attendants to drag him out, and said, "The rebels' execution is not far off—I will first strip them of their courage!"
translations.idiomatic: Geng sent Liu Bingzheng to urge surrender; Chengmo kicked him to the ground, ordered his men to drag Liu out, and said, "The rebels will soon be executed—I will break their spirit first!"

sentences.zh: 」為賊困逾二年，日冠賜冠，衣辭母時衣，遇朔望，奉時憲書一帙懸之，北鄉再拜。

translations.literal: Imprisoned by the rebels for more than two years, he daily wore the court cap bestowed on him and the robe he wore when taking leave of his mother; on the first and fifteenth of the month he hung up a volume of the calendar and bowed twice toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Held by the rebels for more than two years, he daily wore the court cap the emperor had given him and the robe he had worn when bidding his mother farewell; on the first and fifteenth of each month he hung up the calendar and bowed twice toward the north.

sentences.zh: 所居室迫隘，號曰蒙谷。

translations.literal: The room where he lived was cramped; he called it Menggu (Dark Valley).
translations.idiomatic: His cell was cramped; he called it the Dark Valley.

sentences.zh: 為詩文，以桴炭畫壁上。

translations.literal: He composed poetry and prose, using torch charcoal to write on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poems and essays on the walls in charcoal from a torch.

sentences.zh: 時有部曲張福建者，手刃奪門入，連斬數賊，力竭死。

translations.literal: At the time there was a soldier Zhang Fujian who, blade in hand, seized the gate and entered, cut down several rebels in succession, and died when his strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: One of his soldiers, Zhang Fujian, fought his way in with a blade, killed several rebels in succession, and died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人嘛尼為偽散騎郎，精忠遣守承謨，感承謨忠義，謀令出走。

translations.literal: The Mongol Mani served as a false Gentleman Attendant Cavalier; Jingzhong sent him to guard Chengmo; moved by Chengmo's loyalty and righteousness, he plotted to let him escape.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol named Mani held a false post as attendant cavalier; Geng assigned him to guard Chengmo, but moved by Chengmo's loyalty he plotted to help him escape.

sentences.zh: 事泄，精忠將磔之，大言曰：「吾寧與忠臣同死，不原與逆賊同生！

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; Jingzhong was about to dismember him by slow slicing; he spoke loudly: "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!"
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Geng was about to execute him by dismemberment; Mani cried out, "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!"

sentences.zh: 十五年，師克仙霞關，精忠將降，冀飾詞免死，懼承謨暴其罪。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army captured Xianxia Pass; Jingzhong was about to surrender and hoped to use fine words to escape death, fearing Chengmo would expose his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year imperial forces took Xianxia Pass; Geng was about to surrender and hoped to talk his way out of execution, fearing Chengmo would expose his crimes.

sentences.zh: 九月己酉朔，甲子夜半，精忠遣黨偪承謨就​​縊。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, jiyou day of the new moon, at midnight on jiazi, Jingzhong sent his agents to force Chengmo to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on jiazi, the thirteenth day of the ninth month, Geng sent men to force Chengmo to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 幕客嵇永仁、王龍光、沈天成，從弟承譜，下至隸卒，同死者五十三人。

translations.literal: Staff members Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, and Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, down to clerks and runners—fifty-three died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His secretaries Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, and Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, and clerks and runners—fifty-three people died with him.

sentences.zh: 語互詳忠義傳。

translations.literal: Their words are set forth in detail in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Their stories are told at length in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 舊役王道隆奉遣他出，還至延平，聞變，自刎死。

translations.literal: An old servant Wang Daolong had been sent on a mission elsewhere; returning to Yanping, he heard of the uprising and cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: An old retainer, Wang Daolong, had been sent away on business; when he returned to Yanping and heard what had happened, he cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 賊焚承謨屍，棄之野，泰宁騎兵許鼎夜負遺骸藏之。

translations.literal: The rebels burned Chengmo's corpse and cast it in the wild; Taining cavalryman Xu Ding carried the remains away by night and hid them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned Chengmo's body and left it in the open country; a Taining cavalryman named Xu Ding carried the remains away by night and hid them.

sentences.zh: 十六年，喪還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the coffin was returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his coffin was brought back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上遣內大臣侍衛迎奠，贈兵部尚書、太子少保，諡忠貞，御書碑文賜其家。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an Inner Minister and guards to receive and offer libation; he was posthumously made Minister of War and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongzhen (Loyal and Upright), and an imperial inscription for his stele was bestowed on his family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an inner minister and guards to receive the coffin; Chengmo was posthumously made minister of war and junior tutor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Zhongzhen (Loyal Upright), and the emperor wrote a stele inscription for his family.

sentences.zh: 十九年，精忠伏誅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Jingzhong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Geng Jingzhong was executed.

sentences.zh: 赴市曹日，承謨子時崇臠其肉祭墓。

translations.literal: On the day he was taken to the execution ground, Chengmo's son Shichong cut flesh from his body to offer at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Geng was taken to the execution ground, Chengmo's son Shichong cut flesh from the rebel's body as an offering at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 福建民請建祠祀之，御書「忠貞炳日」扁於楣。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian requested to build a shrine to sacrifice to him; the emperor wrote the plaque "Loyal Uprightness Shines Like the Sun" for its lintel.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian asked to build a shrine in his honor; the emperor inscribed its lintel with the words "Loyal Uprightness Shines Like the Sun."

sentences.zh: 承謨所為畫壁集，上親制序。

translations.literal: The collection of wall writings Chengmo composed—the emperor personally wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: For Chengmo's collected writings from his prison walls, the emperor personally wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 時崇，字自牧。

translations.literal: Shichong, whose style name was Zimu.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, styled Zimu.

sentences.zh: 以難廕出知遼陽州，遷直隸順德知府，有惠政。

translations.literal: Through hardship privilege he went out as Zhizhou of Liaoyang, was transferred to be Prefect of Shunde in Zhili, and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Entering office through hardship privilege as prefect of Liaoyang, he later became prefect of Shunde in Zhili and earned a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Fujian Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become Fujian surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，上顧謂群臣曰：「此開國名臣孫，殉難忠臣子也！

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience, the emperor turned and said to the assembled ministers: "This is the grandson of a founding-era eminent minister, the son of a loyal minister who died for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor turned to the court and said, "Here is the grandson of a founding minister and the son of a martyr!"

sentences.zh: 」四十七年，擢廣東巡撫，兼鹽政。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to Governor of Guangdong, concurrently overseeing the salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong with charge of the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢福建浙江總督。

translations.literal: Two years later he was promoted to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，入為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he entered the capital as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was recalled to the capital as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 命出塞築莫代察罕廋爾、鄂爾齋圖杲爾台站凡四十有七所。

translations.literal: He was ordered beyond the passes to build courier stations at Modai Chahan'er, E'erqitu Gao'er, and elsewhere—forty-seven in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered beyond the frontier to build forty-seven courier stations, including those at Modai Chahan'er and E'erqitu Gao'er.

sentences.zh: 又明年，還朝。

translations.literal: The year after that he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 閩人思其德，附祀承謨祠。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian remembered his virtue and joined his sacrifice to Chengmo's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian, remembering his kindness, added him to the sacrifices at Chengmo's shrine.

sentences.zh: =馬雄鎮=馬雄鎮，字錫蕃，漢軍鑲紅旗人，鳴佩子。

translations.literal: Ma Xiongzhen. Ma Xiongzhen, whose style name was Xifan, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner, son of Mingpei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiongzhen, styled Xifan, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner and the son of Mingpei.

sentences.zh: 以廕補工部副理事官，歷遷左僉都御史、國史院學士。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he filled the post of Associate Director in the Board of Works, and was promoted in succession to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Academician of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by hereditary privilege as an associate director in the Ministry of Works, then rose to left vice censor-in-chief and academician of the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year eight he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上，改廣西。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the Shanxi post he was reassigned to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時群盜蝟起，構瑤、僮掠梧州、平樂二府，不數月討平之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere like hedgehogs; Yao and Zhuang were incited to plunder the two prefectures Wuzhou and Pingle, and within a few months he had suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere; Yao and Zhuang raiders ravaged Wuzhou and Pingle, but he suppressed them within a few months.

sentences.zh: 累疏請平鹺價，建學宮，定有司邊俸，省軍糧運費，並罷諸採買累民者，皆得旨允行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting stabilization of salt prices, building of Confucian schools, fixing border stipends for local officials, reducing military grain transport costs, and abolishing all procurement levies that burdened the people—all received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly to stabilize salt prices, build schools, fix frontier officials' pay, cut military grain transport costs, and end burdensome procurement levies—all approved by the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孫延齡以廣西叛應之，圍雄鎮廨，脅降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in response, besieged Xiongzhen's yamen, and coerced him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in support of Wu and besieged Xiongzhen's headquarters, pressing him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫無標​​兵，雄鎮督家人拒守。

translations.literal: At the time the governor had no banner troops; Xiongzhen led his household in holding out.
translations.idiomatic: The governor had no banner troops, so Xiongzhen led his household in defending the compound.

sentences.zh: 密令守備易友亮赴柳州趣提督馬雄來援，弗應。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered Garrison Commander Yi Youliang to go to Liuzhou to urge Military Commander Ma Xiong to come to the rescue; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered garrison commander Yi Youliang to go to Liuzhou and urge commander Ma Xiong to rescue him, but Ma did not respond.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮自經，為家人救免，以蠟丸馳疏請兵。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his household; he sent a memorial in a wax pellet urgently requesting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his family; he then sent an urgent memorial sealed in a wax pellet begging for troops.

sentences.zh: 延齡诇知之，幽雄鎮，置家人別室。

translations.literal: Yanling learned of it through espionage, imprisoned Xiongzhen, and placed his household in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling discovered the plot, imprisoned Xiongzhen, and confined his family separately.

sentences.zh: 三桂使招降，雄鎮不為屈。

translations.literal: Sangui sent men to persuade him to surrender; Xiongzhen would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent envoys to win him over, but Xiongzhen refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 會傅弘烈勸延齡反正，延齡躊躇未決，雄鎮得以間遣長子世濟齎疏詣京師，友亮導之出，客楊啟祥護行，至贛州，江西巡撫董衛國以聞。

translations.literal: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to return to allegiance, Yanling hesitated and had not decided; Xiongzhen seized the interval to send his eldest son Shiji carrying a memorial to the capital; Youliang guided him out, the guest Yang Qixiang escorted the journey; reaching Ganzhou, Jiangxi Governor Dong Weiguo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to defect back to the Qing, Yanling wavered; Xiongzhen used the opening to send his eldest son Shiji to the capital with a memorial. Youliang guided him out, Yang Qixiang escorted him, and at Ganzhou Jiangxi governor Dong Weiguo reported the mission to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上遣使護入京，至，授世濟四品京卿。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to escort him into the capital; on arrival Shiji was made a fourth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent escorts to bring him to the capital and appointed Shiji a fourth-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 居數月，雄鎮又具疏陳粵西可復狀，付長孫國楨，俾與客硃昉鑿垣出。

translations.literal: After several months Xiongzhen again prepared a memorial stating how western Guangdong could be recovered, gave it to his eldest grandson Guozhen, and had him with the guest Zhu Fang break through the wall to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Xiongzhen wrote another memorial on how Guangxi could be recovered, gave it to his grandson Guozhen, and had Zhu Fang help him break through the wall to escape.

sentences.zh: 既，又遣州人唐守道、唐正發潛負次子世永出，次第詣京師。

translations.literal: Afterward he again sent natives of the prefecture Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa secretly to carry out his second son Shiyong, who in turn reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa to smuggle out his second son Shiyong, who also reached the capital in turn.

sentences.zh: 又為延齡知，係其孥於獄。

translations.literal: Yanling learned of this again and imprisoned his wife and children in jail.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling discovered this as well and threw his family into prison.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮憤自剄，復為賊所奪，幽之別室。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen in anger cut his own throat but was again seized by the rebels and confined in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: In fury Xiongzhen cut his own throat, but the rebels seized him again and locked him in another room.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，三桂遣其從孫世琮殺延齡，擁雄鎮至賊壘，迫使降，雄鎮大呼曰：「吾義守封疆，不能寸斬汝以報國，死吾分也！

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Sangui sent his grandnephew Shizong to kill Yanling, escorted Xiongzhen to the rebel camp, and forced him to surrender; Xiongzhen shouted loudly: "By duty I guard the frontier; I could not cut you down inch by inch to repay the state—death is my portion!"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Wu sent his grandnephew Shizong to kill Yanling, dragged Xiongzhen to the rebel camp, and tried to force his surrender. Xiongzhen cried out, "It was my duty to guard the frontier; I could not cut you down to serve the throne—death is all that remains for me!"

sentences.zh: 」賊戕其幼子世洪、世泰怵之，罵益厲，賊殺之，時年四十有四。

translations.literal: The rebels killed his young sons Shihong and Shitai to intimidate him; he cursed all the more fiercely; the rebels killed him; he was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels killed his young sons Shihong and Shitai to frighten him, but he only cursed more fiercely, and they killed him. He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 從者馬雲皋、唐進寶、諸兆元等九人同時死，妻李，妾顧、劉，女二人，世濟妻董、妾苗，並殉。

translations.literal: Followers Ma Yungao, Tang Jinbao, Zhu Zhaoyuan, and nine others died at the same time; his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao—all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Nine followers including Ma Yungao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him; his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, and Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao all perished as well.

sentences.zh: 語互詳列女傳。

translations.literal: Their words are set forth in detail in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: Their stories are told at length in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮屍暴四十馀日，友亮收其骸骨，藁葬焉。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen's corpse was exposed for more than forty days; Youliang collected his bones and gave them a straw burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen's body lay exposed for more than forty days before Youliang gathered his bones and gave them a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮被縶三年，日著書賦詩。

translations.literal: Imprisoned for three years, Xiongzhen daily wrote books and composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Held captive for three years, he wrote and composed poetry every day.

sentences.zh: 既死，客孫成、陳文煥乘間脫走，抵蒼梧，以所著擊笏樓遺稿及匯草辨疑歸世濟。

translations.literal: After his death the guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan seized an interval to escape, reached Cangwu, and returned to Shiji his posthumous writings Jifu Lou Drafts and Huicao Bianyi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan escaped to Cangwu and delivered to Shiji his surviving manuscripts, Jifu Lou Drafts and Huicao Bianyi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，弘烈以雄鎮死狀入告，命議卹。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported Xiongzhen's death to the throne; orders were issued to deliberate on condolence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported Xiongzhen's martyrdom, and the court ordered posthumous honors to be considered.

sentences.zh: 擢世濟大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Shiji was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 成以舉人授同知，文煥授知縣。

translations.literal: Cheng, as a provincial graduate, was made Tongzhi; Wenhuan was made Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng, as a provincial graduate, was made sub-prefect; Chen Wenhuan was made magistrate.

sentences.zh: 旋又授友亮、守道、正發、啟祥游擊、守備有差。

translations.literal: Soon after Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were given posts as Brigadier and Garrison Commander with varying ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were soon given brigadier and garrison commander posts of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 十八年，世濟如廣西迎雄鎮喪至京師，贈太子太傅、兵部尚書，諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring Xiongzhen's coffin to the capital; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous title Wenyi (Cultured and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring his father's coffin to the capital; Xiongzhen was posthumously made grand tutor to the heir apparent and minister of war, with the posthumous name Wenyi (Cultured Resolute).

sentences.zh: 三桂既平，歲正，上宴群臣，特命世濟及陳啟泰子汝器至御座前賜酒。

translations.literal: After Sangui was pacified, on New Year's Day the emperor feasted the ministers and specially ordered Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi before the imperial seat to receive wine.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was defeated, at the New Year feast the emperor summoned Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi before the throne to receive wine.

sentences.zh: 世濟官至遭運總督，世永曆運使；

translations.literal: Shiji rose to Governor of Grain Transport on the Canal; Shiyong became Salt Commissioner of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Shiji rose to canal transport governor; Shiyong became Liang salt commissioner;

sentences.zh: 國楨官江南常鎮道，督餉入藏，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Guozhen held the Chang-Zhen circuit post in Jiangnan, supervised grain transport into Tibet, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen served on the Chang-Zhen circuit in Jiangnan, supervised grain shipments into Tibet, and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: =傅弘烈=傅弘烈，字仲謀，江西進賢人。

translations.literal: Fu Honglie. Fu Honglie, whose style name was Zhongmou, was a native of Jinxian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Honglie, styled Zhongmou, was a native of Jinxian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明末，流寓廣西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he wandered and settled in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming he took refuge in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 順治時，以總督王國光薦，授韶州同知，遷甘肅慶陽知府。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign, on recommendation of Governor Wang Guoguang, he was appointed Tongzhi of Shaozhou and was transferred to be Prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, on Governor Wang Guoguang's recommendation, he became sub-prefect of Shaozhou and later prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂蓄逆謀久，康熙七年，弘烈密以告，逮治，坐誣，論斬。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had long harbored rebellious designs; in the seventh year of Kangxi Honglie secretly reported it; he was arrested and tried, convicted of false accusation, and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had long plotted rebellion; in Kangxi year seven Honglie secretly denounced him, was arrested, convicted of slander, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 九年，上特命減死戍梧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor specially ordered his death sentence reduced and exile to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor commuted the sentence to exile at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及三桂反，將軍孫延齡、提督馬雄以廣西叛應之。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, General Sun Yanling and Military Commander Ma Xiong rebelled in Guangxi in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu rebelled, General Sun Yanling and commander Ma Xiong joined the revolt in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 弘烈欲集兵圖恢復，陽受三桂偽職，入思州、泗城、廣南、富川諸土司，歷交阯界，募義軍得五千人，遂移檄討賊，從尚可喜軍規肇慶。

translations.literal: Honglie wished to gather troops to plan recovery; he outwardly accepted a false post from Sangui, entered the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed the border of Annam, recruited a volunteer army of five thousand men, then issued a proclamation to attack the rebels and followed Shang Kexi's army toward Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie sought to raise troops for recovery; he outwardly accepted a rebel post from Wu, traveled through the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed into Annam, raised five thousand volunteers, issued a call to arms against the rebels, and joined Shang Kexi's advance on Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 三桂甚惎之，使馬雄如柳州害其家百口。

translations.literal: Sangui hated him deeply and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to destroy his household of a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Wu hated him bitterly and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to slaughter his entire family.

sentences.zh: 弘烈說延齡反正。

translations.literal: Honglie persuaded Yanling to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie urged Yanling to return to the Qing side.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕軍贛州，弘烈密致書言延齡妻孔四貞，定南王有德女，未忘國恩，延齡可招撫。

translations.literal: Southern Pacification General Jueluo Shushu was at Ganzhou with his army; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Youde, had not forgotten the state's grace and Yanling could be won over.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Pacification General Jueluo Shushu was at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Youde, still remembered the dynasty's kindness and that Yanling could be won back.

sentences.zh: 又致書奉詔招撫督捕理事官麻勒吉，言王師速進南安，弘烈自韶州策應，則兩粵可定。

translations.literal: He also wrote to the Imperial Commissioner for Pacification and Capture Meleji, saying that if the imperial army quickly advanced to Nan'an and Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, the two Guang provinces could be secured.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to pacification commissioner Meleji, urging the imperial army to advance quickly on Nan'an while Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, so that both Guang provinces could be recovered.

sentences.zh: 舒恕、麻勒吉先後以聞，上嘉其忠誠，授廣西巡撫、徵蠻滅寇將軍，俾增募義兵，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Shushu and Meleji reported in succession; the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him Governor of Guangxi and General for Subduing Barbarians and Destroying Bandits, allowing him to recruit more volunteers and act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Shushu and Meleji reported his letters in turn; the emperor praised his loyalty and made him governor of Guangxi and general for subduing rebels, with authority to raise more volunteers and act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 弘烈克梧州，下昭平、賀、鬱林、博白、北流、陸川、興業諸州縣，進复潯州，遣平樂知府劉曉齎疏上方略。

translations.literal: Honglie captured Wuzhou, took the prefectures and counties Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, and Xingye, advanced to recover Xunzhou, and sent Pingle Prefect Liu Xiao to carry a memorial reporting strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie took Wuzhou, then Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, and Xingye, recovered Xunzhou, and sent Pingle prefect Liu Xiao to the capital with a strategic memorial.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保，並加曉參議道。

translations.literal: On review of merit he was given the additional title Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and Liu Xiao was given the additional post of Participation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made junior guardian to the heir apparent, and Liu Xiao was promoted to participation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 當是時，馬雄據柳州，三桂諸將分據平樂、南寧、橫州，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou; Sangui's generals held Pingle, Nanning, and Hengzhou separately—the momentum was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou and Wu's generals held Pingle, Nanning, and Hengzhou—the rebel position looked formidable.

sentences.zh: 弘烈雖屢捷，惟新軍缺砲馬，假於尚之信，弗應。

translations.literal: Although Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked cannon and horses; he borrowed from Shang Zhixin, who did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Though Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked artillery and horses; he asked Shang Zhixin for help, but Shang refused.

sentences.zh: 吳世琮既殺延齡，陷平樂，襲弘烈梧州，弘烈擊敗之。

translations.literal: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling, took Pingle, and attacked Honglie at Wuzhou, Honglie defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling, seized Pingle, and attacked Honglie at Wuzhou, Honglie drove him off.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與將軍莽依圖圍平樂，戰失利，弘烈與互訐。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he joined General Mangyitu in besieging Pingle; the battle went badly and Honglie and Mangyitu accused each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he joined General Mangyitu in besieging Pingle; the attack failed and the two men exchanged accusations.

sentences.zh: 詔謂弘烈兵未支俸餉，奮勇收復諸路。

translations.literal: An edict said Honglie's troops had not yet received stipends or rations yet had bravely recovered many routes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Honglie's troops had fought without pay yet bravely recovered many districts.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖自平樂退賀縣，又言糧乏，再退梧州，使弘烈所复郡縣盡棄於賊，因飭莽依圖圖效。

translations.literal: Mangyitu retreated from Pingle to Hexian, again citing lack of grain, retreated again to Wuzhou, causing all the prefectures and counties Honglie had recovered to be abandoned to the rebels; he was therefore ordered to urge Mangyitu to achieve results.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu withdrew from Pingle to Hexian, then citing lack of supplies fell back to Wuzhou, leaving all the districts Honglie had recovered to the rebels; the court ordered Mangyitu to show results.

sentences.zh: 弘烈督兵進，賊數万渡左江，弘烈戰敗。

translations.literal: Honglie led troops forward; tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River; Honglie was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie advanced, but tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 賊陷藤縣，逼梧州。

translations.literal: The rebels took Teng County and pressed on Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Teng County and threatened Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，之信軍至，弘烈分兵水陸，乘賊攻城時三面夾擊，賊潰​​走，遂下藤縣，克平樂，進复桂林。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived; Honglie divided forces by land and water, and while the rebels were attacking the city struck them from three sides; the rebels broke and fled; he then took Teng County, captured Pingle, and advanced to recover Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived; Honglie split his forces by land and water and, while the rebels were besieging the city, struck them from three sides; the rebels broke and fled; he retook Teng County, captured Pingle, and advanced to recover Guilin.

sentences.zh: 弘烈密疏言延齡舊部宜善為解散，又言之信怙惡反覆，當早為之所。

translations.literal: Honglie secretly memorialized that Yanling's old troops should be properly disbanded, and also that Zhixin relied on past evil and was changeable—measures should be taken against him early.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie secretly memorialized that Yanling's old troops should be properly disbanded and warned that Zhixin was treacherous and unreliable and should be dealt with early.

sentences.zh: 馬雄死，子承廕仍附三桂，受偽封懷寧公，詭言乞款附，弘烈許之，為疏聞。

translations.literal: Ma Xiong died; his son Chengyin still adhered to Sangui, received the false title Duke of Huaining, falsely claimed to beg to submit, Honglie agreed, and memorialized to report it.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Xiong died, his son Chengyin still served Wu, took the false title Duke of Huaining, and pretended to seek surrender; Honglie agreed and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 詔授承廕昭義將軍統其眾。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chengyin General of Manifest Righteousness to command his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Chengyin general of manifest righteousness to command his troops.

sentences.zh: 弘烈規取雲、貴。

translations.literal: Honglie planned to take Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie planned to advance into Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，次柳州，承廕期弘烈會議，弘烈至，承廕以其眾叛，襲破其營，執送貴陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year he halted at Liuzhou; Chengyin arranged a meeting with Honglie; when Honglie arrived Chengyin rebelled with his troops, stormed and broke his camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year he camped at Liuzhou; Chengyin arranged a meeting, then rebelled with his troops, overran Honglie's camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世璠誘以偽職，弘烈曰：「爾祖未反時，吾已劾奏，料汝家必為叛逆。

translations.literal: Shifan tempted him with a false post; Honglie said, "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already memorialized impeaching him; I foresaw your house would surely turn traitor."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan offered him a rebel post; Honglie said, "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already denounced him to the throne; I knew your family would turn traitor."

sentences.zh: 汝敢以此言污我邪？

translations.literal: How dare you use such words to defile me?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you try to stain me with such talk?"

sentences.zh: 」世琮百計說之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: Shizong tried every means to persuade him; he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong tried every means to win him over, but Honglie only cursed more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 十月辛丑，遇害。

translations.literal: On xinchou day of the tenth month he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month, he was murdered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，征南將軍穆佔复貴陽，收遺骸，以死狀聞，贈太子太師、兵部尚書，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Southern Expedition General Muzhan recovered Guiyang, collected the remains, reported his death; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Southern Expedition General Muzhan recovered Guiyang, gathered Honglie's remains, and reported his martyrdom; Honglie was posthumously made grand preceptor to the heir apparent and minister of war, with the posthumous name Zhongyi (Loyal Resolute).

sentences.zh: 二十二年，允廣西巡撫郝浴請，建雙忠祠於桂林，祀弘烈及馬雄鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, granting Guangxi Governor Hao Yu's request, the Double Loyalty Shrine was built at Guilin to sacrifice to Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, on Guangxi governor Hao Yu's request, the Double Loyalty Shrine was built in Guilin to honor Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：方諸籓盛強，朝廷所置督撫，勢不足以相抗。

translations.literal: Commentary says: When the feudatories were at the height of their power, the governors and governors-general the court placed in office did not have strength enough to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the feudatories were at their strongest, the governors the court appointed were not strong enough to stand against them.

sentences.zh: 文焜雖與三桂分疆而治，所部貳於三桂久矣。

translations.literal: Although Wenkun governed a separate territory from Sangui, his subordinates had long been disloyal to Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Although Wenkun governed a separate territory from Wu Sangui, his troops had long been loyal to Wu instead.

sentences.zh: 若承謨之於精忠，雄鎮之於延齡，皆同城逼處，惟以身殉，無他術也。

translations.literal: As with Chengmo toward Jingzhong and Xiongzhen toward Yanling—all were pressed in the same city and had no method but to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: As with Chengmo against Geng Jingzhong and Xiongzhen against Sun Yanling—all lived in the same city as the rebel and had no recourse but martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 弘烈異軍特起，又與莽依圖相失，勢孤，遂困於承廕。

translations.literal: Honglie rose as a separate force, but also fell out with Mangyitu; isolated in strength, he was finally trapped by Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie arose as an independent force but fell out with Mangyitu; isolated, he was finally trapped by Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 要其忠義激烈，作士氣，怵寇心，皆不為徒死者。

translations.literal: Essentially their fierce loyalty and righteousness roused the spirit of scholars, awed the hearts of bandits—they did not die in vain.
translations.idiomatic: In the end their fierce loyalty inspired others, shook the rebels, and none of them died in vain.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，烈已！

translations.literal: Alas, how fierce!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how fierce their devotion!
